gate.reason: Two human calls, neither of them authority — `architecture.md` puts the module list in the tree's hands, so plan does not need a Decision to name `src/lock.rs`. (1) Sequencing and cost: a behavior-neutral ~2090-line move whose fence spans 59 existing files (15 `src/`, 42 `tests/it/`, `drift.rs`, and the one re-blessed `ts-rs` binding) beside the new `src/lock.rs` can share a wave with nothing, so it runs alone against a drained queue and buys churn against no test that could go red — whether to buy it at all is the human's. (2) Where the row→model lifts at the codec's tail land — `nested_members_from_rows` 6274 over `embedded_member_from_row` 6288, `requirement_from_row` 6311, `clause_from_row` 6339, `edges_from_declarations` 6356 over `edge_column` 6385, `mention_edges_from_declarations` 6396, `import_edges_from_doc` 6414: recommended answer is beside the model type they produce — `compose`/`graph`/`extract`, which is where `compose::clause_from_row` (407) already lives and what `drift::clause_from_row`'s thin delegation to it already implies — leaving `lock.rs` a codec with no model dependency. A ruling the other way (the lifts ride the codec) is one word in this entry.

new.description: The flat module (`architecture.md`, "The tree stays flat": a split lands as a new flat module) owning the lock declaration codec moved from `src/drift.rs` 4338-6427 — its section banner (4338-4340), `Declarations` (4361) and every `*Row` type, their `*_table`/`*_from_table` TOML round-trip pairs, the column readers (`req_str` 5339, `opt_str` 5344, `opt_table` 5406), `LockRowError` (719)/`RowError`, and the read/parse door (`read_lock_document` 5174, `read_declarations` 5211, `read_engine` 5228, `engine_from_doc` 5238, `parse_declarations` 5254, `declarations_from_doc` 5276). A move, not a rewrite: no signature, no behavior, no row column changes, and `drift` imports it rather than re-exporting it — one door per name, never two (`engineering.md`, "An export earns its consumer"). One byte of prose is not verbatim: `Declarations`'s doc (4353) names `GATE-READ-LOCK-DEMOLITION` as "next in the chain", a tag retired at ce61d85c — the clause goes, the sentence keeping the fact that `import`'s extraction still writes this family for the `check` path it feeds.

edit.description: Keeps the emit compiler (`emit_program` 1380 → `emit` 1490 → `emit_one` 3040 / `emit_manifest` 2229 / `project_bytes` 3189), the manifest-path and kind-fact helpers beside it (`manifest_target_path` 2131, `manifest_path_for` 2141, `manifest_owner_label` 2156, `ownerless_manifest_label` 2178, `kind_facts_over_floor` 2199 — facts→path resolution is emit-side, so they stay), `place` (3341) and the lock read verbs (`config_stale` 3428 over `config_stale_from_doc` 3442, `undeclared_layout_members_from_doc` 3534, `undeclared_locus_members_from_doc` 3627, the source-dep row families 3682-4064 and their four faces — `source_dep_stale_from_doc` 4065, `layout_import_stale_from_doc` 4147, `include_stale_from_doc` 4188, `input_stale_from_doc` 4231 — and `emit_owned_targets` 4276 over `emit_owned_targets_from_doc` 4287). The declaration codec (4338-6427) moves out, and the header doc (1-14) — which already describes emit, drift and place alone — becomes true of the file.

`ts-rs` projects `Declarations`'s Rust doc comment into this committed binding, so the retired-tag clause the move drops is mirrored here (26) and the file is re-blessed with it: `BLESS_SEAM_BINDINGS=1 cargo test --test it seam_bindings` (the header of `tests/it/seam_bindings_current.rs`), never a hand edit. The move itself changes no other generated byte — `ts-rs` keys a binding by type name, not module path.

summary: src/drift.rs carries three jobs in 6766 lines; the lock declaration codec (~2090 of them) splits to a flat src/lock.rs, drift keeping emit + place

tests.asserts: the codec's own round-trip suite passes unchanged against `src/lock.rs` — the move's one proof, since nothing here is a behavior claim

the ts-rs export byte-compare is green after re-blessing, with `Declarations.ts`'s doc comment the only generated file to change — the bindings are keyed by type name, not module path, so the move itself stops at the Rust side

acceptance: cargo test, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all --check and the rustdoc gate green; `src/lock.rs` owns the declaration codec, `src/drift.rs`'s header describes everything the file still holds, no consumer reaches a codec symbol through `drift`, and `git diff --stat` shows `sdk/src/generated/` changed in `Declarations.ts` alone.
